title: Get READY for Election Week Chaos (3 Stocks That Win Anyway)
creator: MarketBeat
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; auto-captions garble names/numbers in places
summary: MarketBeat analyst Chris Marcotte pitches three green-energy names as buys that win regardless of the election outcome, arguing the story is now demand-driven, not policy-driven. Investors wrongly treat green energy as subsidy-dependent, he says; the real driver is hyperscalers and neo-clouds struggling to power data centres efficiently without harming local communities, and companies solving that problem today benefit. Nuclear is explicitly excluded — it may have its day, but not now. Bloom Energy (BE) sells on-site fuel cells solving data centres' power problem today: a third-quarter beat ($0.94 versus $0.69 expected, revenue $1.24 billion versus $1.07 billion), now GAAP-profitable, and he would not exit after a 20% pullback despite a 161% year-to-date gain. Ecolab (ECL) serves data-centre water and liquid-cooling needs: third-quarter organic sales up 13%, EPS $2.18 (up 5%), a consensus target implying over 10% upside, and a 33-year dividend record ($2.92 per year). Brookfield Renewable (BEP) offers hydro, wind, solar and storage breadth, a 10,500 MW framework deal with Microsoft plus about 3,000 MW of hydro with Alphabet, and a 5.39% yield ($1.57 per year) under $30 — with a note that its MLP structure means extra tax forms. Calls: BE — BUY (reiterated), ECL — BUY (first tracked), BEP — BUY (first tracked).
